answer_text:
We want the degree of the splitting field \(T\) of

\[
f(x)=x^3+18x+3
\]

over \(\mathbb{Q}\).

### 1. Check irreducibility over \(\mathbb{Q}\)

Since \(f\) is a monic cubic with integer coefficients, if it has a rational root it must be one of

\[
\pm 1,\ \pm 3.
\]

Check:

\[
f(1)=1+18+3=22,
\]
\[
f(-1)=-1-18+3=-16,
\]
\[
f(3)=27+54+3=84,
\]
\[
f(-3)=-27-54+3=-78.
\]

None are zero, so \(f(x)\) has no rational root. Since it has degree \(3\), this implies \(f(x)\) is irreducible over \(\mathbb{Q}\).

Thus if \(\alpha\) is a root,

\[
[\mathbb{Q}(\alpha):\mathbb{Q}]=3.
\]

### 2. Compute the discriminant

For a depressed cubic

\[
x^3+px+q,
\]

the discriminant is

\[
\Delta=-4p^3-27q^2.
\]

Here \(p=18\) and \(q=3\), so

\[
\Delta=-4(18)^3-27(3)^2.
\]

Compute:

\[
18^3=5832,
\]

so

\[
\Delta=-4(5832)-27(9)
=-23328-243
=-23571.
\]

Thus

\[
\Delta=-23571.
\]

In particular, \(\Delta\) is not a square in \(\mathbb{Q}\). Also, \(\Delta\neq 0\), so \(f\) is separable.

### 3. Determine the Galois group

Because \(f(x)\) is irreducible of degree \(3\), its Galois group is a transitive subgroup of \(S_3\). The only possibilities are

\[
C_3 \cong A_3
\]

or

\[
S_3.
\]

For an irreducible cubic over \(\mathbb{Q}\), the Galois group is \(A_3\) if and only if the discriminant is a square in \(\mathbb{Q}\). Since

\[
\Delta=-23571
\]

is not a square in \(\mathbb{Q}\), the Galois group must be

\[
S_3.
\]

### 4. Degree of the splitting field

The splitting field \(T\) has degree over \(\mathbb{Q}\) equal to the order of the Galois group:

\[
[T:\mathbb{Q}] = |S_3| = 6.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\boxed{6}
\]
